Reviewed all 50 verbs in shard 0; wrote findings for 9 to `verbdata/gloss-review/shards/gloss_000.out.json`.

| Verb | Shipped | Severity | Proposed |
|---|---|---|---|
| abberufen | withdraw | medium | recall from a post |
| abblasen | blow off something, blow clear | medium | call off, cancel |
| abdrehen | veer | medium | turn off, shut off |
| abfeiern | celebrate, praise, love | medium | take time off in lieu |
| abführen | take away | low | lead away (in custody) |
| abgleichen | verify congruence | low | compare, reconcile |
| abhauen | cut off | medium | clear off, run away |
| ablenken | divert | medium | distract, divert |
| ablesen | read | medium | read off (a meter) |

Six of the nine are mechanical import defects with the correct sense already sitting at a named `candidate_glosses` index; the other three (`abführen`, `abgleichen`, `ablesen`) are shortening damage.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The `ablesen` case shows why the "shortening mangled it" class is hard to catch by rule: dropping "(take a reading)" left a *grammatical, plausible* gloss — it just collapsed the prefixed verb onto its base verb. A cheap machine check for this class would be flagging any separable verb whose gloss is a substring-equal match to its base verb's gloss.
- `abhauen` and `abdrehen` are both cases where the literal, compositional sense (hew off, turn away) is listed first because it's etymologically prior, while usage has moved to a figurative sense. kaikki's entry order tracks historical layering, not frequency — which is exactly the bias described in the brief.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
